items.title: How do I choose a renderer, and how do they work?
items.description:
Choose a renderer under Settings → Video Settings → Renderer (only when the game is not running):

• Zink translates OpenGL through the system Vulkan stack (GL→Vulkan→Metal). It suits newer 26.x versions and modded instances, with smoother chunk loading.
• MobileGlues translates OpenGL to Metal. It is compatible and suits lighter workloads and older versions, but incurs more translation work per frame during chunk loading; this is also known on Android.
• LTW is a lightweight OpenGL 3.3-to-ES translation layer shared with Android. It has low overhead and suits lightweight versions through 1.21.x, but does not support MC 26.x (see below).
• Krypton Wrapper (≤26.2, formerly NG-GL4ES) is the same gl4es renderer used by ZL2. It translates shaders in two stages with glslang and SPIRV-Cross and is reported to work with nearly all MC versions. Use it as the VGPU replacement on older versions when textures are corrupted or atlases misaligned.
• gl4es (≤26.2) is the traditional gl4es renderer from the ZL2 launcher (PojavLauncherTeam fork, built from source). Its lightweight C shader converter rewrites shader strings and has no extra shader-pipeline dependencies. It is an alternative to Krypton Wrapper for older versions; holy gl4es was removed this round and replaced here.
• MoltenVK maps the Vulkan API directly to Metal as a standalone renderer. On MC 26.2+, select Vulkan under the in-game Video Settings → Graphics menu to use it; with FPS unlocking, frame rates can exceed the display refresh rate. It is independent of Zink, which uses the system Vulkan stack.
• Auto lets the launcher choose a renderer based on the game version.

In short: use Zink for newer versions and modpacks; prefer Krypton Wrapper for older versions (try gl4es ≤26.2 if needed, or MobileGlues/LTW for lighter workloads); choose MoltenVK when you need Vulkan.

items.title: Does the game crash immediately with LTW on MC 26.x?
items.description:
This is a known capability limit. The launcher checks before launch and displays a warning and blocks startup if LTW is selected for MC 26.x.

On iOS, LTW translates desktop OpenGL 3.3 through Apple's GLES 3.0 backend. MC 26.x cloud rendering requires texture buffers (`samplerBuffer`), a core desktop GL 3.1 feature unavailable in ES 3.0. Cloud shaders therefore fail to compile and the game crashes at the title screen. Typical logs include `samplerBuffer: Illegal use of reserved word` and `Failed to load required shader programs: pipeline/flat_clouds`.

Fix: under Settings → Video Settings → Renderer, select Zink or MobileGlues. Both fully support 26.x: Zink provides desktop-class GL 4.x, while MobileGlues includes texture-buffer emulation.

LTW remains usable through 1.21.x. Adding texture-buffer emulation to LTW is structural work and is on the roadmap, following the similar emulation layer in MobileGlues.

items.title: What is Krypton Wrapper (formerly NG-GL4ES), and how does it relate to VGPU and gl4es?
items.description:
Krypton Wrapper (≤26.2, formerly NG-GL4ES) is a gl4es fork used by ZalithLauncher 2. It translates desktop OpenGL to OpenGL ES and converts shaders in two stages: glslang (GLSL→SPIR-V) followed by SPIRV-Cross (SPIR-V→ESSL). Its pipeline differs from VGPU's built-in conversion pipeline.

When to use it:
• On older versions (such as the 1.8.9 Forge ecosystem), if VGPU causes corrupted textures, misaligned atlases, or stripes (a translation-layer issue not resolved by two rounds of fixes), Krypton Wrapper is the preferred alternative.
• It is reported to work with nearly all MC versions; try it on newer 26.x versions too, and switch to Zink if it fails.
• Advanced options can be placed in `config.json` under the game's `ngg/` folder; most users do not need them.

Select it at Settings → Video Settings → Renderer → Krypton Wrapper (≤26.2). The game must not be running when you change renderers.

items.title: Is stuttering while MobileGlues loads chunks normal?
items.description:
Yes; this is a known behavior. MobileGlues translates OpenGL to Metal, and the new 26.x chunk pipeline places heavier demands on it: at the same view distance, translation calls are about three times higher than in older versions, so frame rates can drop noticeably while moving. MobileGlues also stutters on Android because of the upstream translation stack's inherent overhead.

Ways to reduce it, in order of value:
1. Use the direct Vulkan backend (MobileGL) and enable an FSR preset (recommended since Task166; smoothest during chunk loading).
2. Switch to Zink for substantially higher chunk-streaming throughput.
3. Enable FSR upscaling to lower the render resolution (see below).
4. Keep view distance around 10; increasing it mainly lengthens chunk-loading spikes.

GC, memory capacity, and GPU performance have been ruled out as causes. Simply allocating more memory will not fix this stutter.

items.title: How do I use FSR upscaling, and which renderers support it?
items.description:
Choose a preset under Settings → Video Settings → FSR 1.0 Upscaling: Ultra Quality 77%, Quality 67%, Balanced 59%, or Performance 50%. The game renders at a lower resolution and FSR's EASU algorithm scales the image back to full screen, noticeably improving frame rate with a small reduction in image quality.

Supported renderers (multi-renderer support was added recently):
• MobileGlues: FSR1 is built in and is the most mature option. This is the GLES and OpenGL 4.0 backend of the mg renderer; preset synchronization works directly on the same path since Task158.
• Zink: Uses the same EASU upscaling before presentation. Earlier builds had green artifacts and image splitting, both fixed. The first issue was GLSL 4.1 compatibility and missing half-precision functions; the second was an incorrect order of upscaling and readback. The current path upscales before readback and explicitly locks the default framebuffer.
• The mg direct Vulkan backend (MobileGL): Supported since Tasks166/167. The Metal presentation layer intercepts and upscales the image; full FSR1 (EASU+RCAS) was validated on-device.
• Other renderers (MoltenVK, Auto, gl4es, etc.): Not supported yet.

Notes:
1. Leave the resolution slider at 100%; lowering it manually would apply scaling a second time.
2. Earlier issues (black screen after enabling, image confined to the lower-left, and green artifacts in Zink) have been fixed through shader fallback, viewport detection, and GLSL compatibility/half-precision fixes. If they recur, send the log.
3. FSR upscales the completed game frame once, with very little overhead. If enabling FSR seems to cause stutter, it is probably chunk-loading lag (see the MobileGlues entry), not FSR.

items.title: Can MetalFX Temporal upscaling replace FSR?
items.description:
Short answer: Temporal upscaling is not currently feasible because of a hard engine-level dependency, not because the launcher is unwilling to support it.

Why it is not feasible:
MetalFX Temporal requires the game to provide per-pixel motion vectors (required by the API), a depth map, camera jitter, and a reprojection matrix every frame. Vanilla Minecraft's rendering pipeline does not produce motion vectors; adding them requires changes inside the game's renderer at the engine/mod level (comparable to Sodium/Iris in scope). The launcher's presentation bridge sees only the final frame and has no depth or camera data, so it cannot synthesize correct motion vectors. Temporal accumulation without them would cause severe ghosting, and Apple's API requires this input.

What about the Spatial version?
MetalFX Spatial and FSR 1.0 are both single-frame upscalers with similar image quality. MetalFX also requires iOS 16+ and A13+ devices and an extra texture-interoperability layer, for little marginal benefit, so it is not being added for now.

Recommendation: For frame rate, use FSR Ultra Quality/Quality with Zink or MobileGlues. For image quality, disable FSR and render natively. If upstream (Sodium or Mojang) provides motion vectors in the future, Temporal upscaling will be reconsidered.

items.title: Can Arm ASR (Arm Accuracy Super Resolution) replace FSR?
items.description:
Not for now. Unlike MetalFX Temporal, Arm ASR does not require motion vectors; like FSR 1.0, it is a single-frame spatial upscaler derived from FSR1. The obstacles are implementation and limited expected benefit.

Why it cannot be used as-is:
Arm's official implementation uses Vulkan/DX12 compute shaders. Zink exposes OpenGL 4.1 to the game, which lacks compute shaders (they require 4.3), so the reference implementation will not run unchanged. Porting it would require rewriting the algorithm as fragment shaders, as with the launcher's FSR.

Why the gain would be small:
Arm ASR's performance advantage comes from compute-shader tiling and shared-memory access tuned for Mali GPUs. Those optimizations do not help Apple GPUs through a fragment pipeline; image quality would also differ little from FSR1 because both derive from FSR1.

Recommendation: Enable FSR on Zink; recent builds add GLSL 4.1 adaptation, automatic version fallback, and missing half-precision packing functions. If native Vulkan/Metal presentation with compute-shader support is added later, ASR and MetalFX Spatial will be reevaluated.

items.title: What alternatives to FSR 1.0 are available, and why was it chosen?
items.description:
For single-frame spatial upscaling, these are the alternatives and tradeoffs (based on public evaluations and source research from 2024–2025):

NVIDIA NIS (Image Scaling): Open source (MIT), combines scaling and sharpening in one pass, and supports multiple GPU vendors. Public comparisons find image quality nearly identical to FSR 1; a single pass may use less bandwidth. It is the only comparable alternative worth considering, but integration would require GLSL adaptation similar in scope to the completed FSR work.

Qualcomm GSR (Game Super Resolution): Open source (BSD-3), single-pass spatial upscaling. Its main benefit is wave-occupancy tuning for Adreno GPUs; those optimizations do not help Apple GPUs, and image quality is similar to FSR1, so switching offers no gain.

Apple MetalFX Spatial: Digital Foundry's tests on the Mac version of Resident Evil found lower image quality than FSR 1 in the same engine and spatial-upscaling category. Integration also requires iOS 16+, an A13+ device, and an extra texture-interoperability layer.

Anime4K/FSRCNNX and other video algorithms target edge reconstruction in animation; results in general 3D scenes are inconsistent and compute cost is higher, so they are unsuitable for real-time game upscaling.

Temporal algorithms (DLSS, FSR 2–3, XeSS, MetalFX Temporal, Arm ASR) have a higher image-quality ceiling, but all depend on engine-provided motion vectors, depth, and jitter sequences. The launcher cannot synthesize these inputs; see the MetalFX and Arm ASR entries above.

Conclusion: FSR 1's EASU is already a top-tier single-frame spatial upscaler, and some tests find it better than MetalFX Spatial. Zink's GL 4.1 adaptation is complete, so the risk of switching outweighs the gains from a comparable algorithm. A real image-quality leap requires temporal inputs.

items.title: How do I adjust the frame-rate limit and VSync?
items.description:
• Frame-rate limit: In-game Video Settings → Max Framerate (the launcher Java arguments also expose the `-Dmax.fps` unlock). Choose Unlimited or a high value.
• VSync: Turn it off under in-game Video Settings → VSync. Renderers then present immediately instead of waiting for refresh, benefiting high-refresh-rate devices.
• 26.x modpacks limited to 30 FPS during loading/inactivity: MC 26.3 added inactivity throttling. AFK mode defaults to 30 FPS after 60 seconds without input and 10 FPS after 10 minutes; no-touch modpack loading triggers it. Fixed in Task104 by writing `inactivityFpsLimit=minimized` and injecting a zero-delta scroll heartbeat every 45 seconds. Log marker: `[InputDiag] Task104 AFK heartbeat`. If heavy gameplay remains near 30 FPS, lower view distance (≤16 recommended for large modpacks) and the FSR preset.
• 26.x Zink+FSR steady at 29–30 FPS (Task106 diagnosis): Increasing FSR from 1.3x to 2.0x (58% fewer rendered pixels) did not change frame rate. The bottleneck was two full-frame GPU→CPU readbacks per frame plus row-flip copying. Task106 bundle-direct uses two sentinels to confirm that the driver's buffer contains the full frame, then skips the duplicate readback and row flip and presents that buffer directly. Log marker: `[OSMBridge] Task106 bundle-direct present engaged`. Heartbeat timings identify `t=swap` (launcher total), `[pre+easu / glFinish / readback]` (phase timings), `frame` (full frame period), and `MC-side = frame - swap` (game time). If MC-side dominates, lower view distance or change renderers; if glFinish/readback dominates, send the log for further presentation-path optimization.
• "Modpack at 30 FPS but vanilla is fine" (Task110 root cause): The `dynamic-fps` mod, often bundled with modpacks (3.11.10 in this case), throttles the game when it thinks the window is unfocused. Vanilla does not include it; the game itself is always considered focused. Fixed in Task110: SDL window flags now always report focused and visible (embedded game view is the foreground on iOS; rendering is frozen in the background anyway), so the mod's state machine stays in its normal focused/unlimited mode. Log marker: `[SDLHook] Task110`. Other background-throttling mods such as IdleHandler are covered too.
• If the frame rate is still low, identify the bottleneck: GPU saturation (lower view distance/enable FSR) or chunk-loading lag (switch to Zink/lower view distance).
• If frame rate fluctuates but the average is not low, chunk-streaming spikes are likely; see the MobileGlues entry.

items.title: How can I fix a blurry or soft image?
items.description:
Common causes and fixes:

1. FSR preset is too low (Balanced/Performance): try Ultra Quality or compare with FSR disabled.
2. The resolution slider was lowered manually: restore it to 100% (use an FSR preset for lower resolution; image quality is much better).
3. The 1x scaling blur in older builds has been fixed (render surface now matches physical pixels 1:1); report it if it returns.
4. UI scale is too low: increase it under in-game Video Settings → GUI Scale.
5. Sodium Extra's "Lower Resolution on Mac" option: In packs with Sodium Extra (such as BMC2), enabling Video Settings → Sodium Extra → Performance → Lower Resolution on Mac in the launcher's macOS-emulation environment halves the framebuffer and scales it back to full screen. A measured 590x410 render was upscaled to 2360x1640 (4x), making it visibly blurry. This is a mod setting, not a launcher issue; turn it off to restore full-resolution rendering, or leave it on/use FSR for higher frame rate.

Tip: To tell blur from low resolution, zoom in on a screenshot: jagged block edges indicate low resolution; a hazy image indicates filtering/scaling.

items.title: Can I install shaders (Iris/OptiFine) and optimization mods? What should I watch out for?
items.description:
Yes, but version matching is essential and is a common cause of crashes:

1. Iris is tightly coupled to a specific Sodium version. Updating only one can produce "Some of your mods are incompatible"; update them together or use the versions recommended by the launcher.
2. Sodium for 26.x may have additional dependencies such as Sodium Options API. If the error mentions dependency conflicts, add or align the required versions.
3. OptiFine conflicts with Sodium/Iris; do not install them together.
4. Shaders are demanding on the GPU. Test with low/medium presets first; after confirming stability, try more demanding ones. Zink + FSR is recommended when shaders are enabled.
5. If the game crashes after installing mods, check the crash report's "Caused by" section (available in the in-game menu). In most cases, versions do not match; it is usually not a launcher issue.

items.title: With a 1.20.x modpack, Zink, and FSR enabled, is the image confined to the lower-left with large blank areas?
items.description:
Typical symptom: With Zink selected and an FSR preset enabled, the game starts and remains playable, but the image occupies only about two-thirds of the lower-left screen area, leaving the rest blank.

Mechanism: With FSR enabled, the game renders at a reduced resolution into the lower-left of a full-size buffer, then an upscaling pass expands it to full screen. This path was verified on MC 26.3, but in some 1.20.x modpacks (such as BMC2) the upscaled result did not reach the final readback buffer; the raw low-resolution frame was presented in the corner.

Fixed through Tasks99–105: Task99 detection, Task100 authoritative presentation, Task103 ground-truth verification, Task104 far-corner sentinel, and Task105 viewport adaptation. Presentation no longer relies on the driver's `glFinish` readback; the launcher reads the authoritative framebuffer each frame and presents it independently. Two corner sentinels verify full-screen coverage: the lower-left sentinel alone only proves that an upscaled fragment exists, while the opposite lower-right sentinel (screen upper-right) confirms full-frame rasterization. If both are present, EASU covered the frame; if either is missing, the original game image is immediately stretched to full screen by Core Animation. Task105 also reads the actual game viewport every frame instead of assuming the window size reported to the launcher, so the upscaler follows modpacks that change the presentation region.

To verify, search the log for `[OSMBridge] Task103 EASU sentinel verdict`: `LANDED` means both sentinels were hit and EASU presented the full frame; `NOT LANDED` means the stretch fallback is active. `far=N/M` reports the far-corner sentinel hits. `[OSMBridge] Task105 viewport evidence` compares the actual game viewport to the reported window size (`DIVERGED` means adaptive handling took over), and `[OSMBridge] Task104 EASU viewport check` shows the viewport held by the driver.

Temporary workaround on older builds: Settings → Video Settings → FSR 1.0 Upscaling → Off. The game then renders at native resolution with a lower frame rate.

items.title: How do I type in-game (chat, commands, names), and what is the difference between the two keyboard buttons?
items.description:
First, open a text field before typing: tap the chat button or press T to open chat.

The two keyboard buttons have different functions:

[System keyboard] ✎ icon ("Input Method" button)
Opens the iOS software keyboard, including Chinese input, suggestions, and emoji. Use either:
1. Tap the "✎ Input Method" button in the control layout (tap it again to dismiss the keyboard).
2. Long-press the screen with two fingers (first enable Settings → Controls → Two-finger keyboard shortcut).

[Button keyboard] ⌨ icon ("Keyboard" drawer)
Opens a full key panel (QWERTY, symbols, and function keys). Letters go directly to the game without opening the system keyboard:
• Hold SHIFT while pressing a letter to capitalize; the Caps Lock button toggles capitalization.
• SHIFT modifies symbol keys (for example, SHIFT+, produces <).
• Holding Ctrl/Alt while pressing a letter invokes shortcut behavior instead of entering text, just like a physical keyboard.

Troubleshooting:
1. If letters do nothing, check that chat is open (press T or tap the chat button).
2. The ⌨ panel was unresponsive in early builds because its background intercepted touches; this is fixed. If an older installation still has the issue after updating, choose "Restore Default Controls" in the control editor to get the latest factory layout.
3. If a particular key behaves incorrectly (for example, a symbol is misplaced), your custom layout may have changed its mapping; restore the default controls.
4. If the issue remains, send the log; it records each button press.

items.title: Does the joystick not respond, or only work while Shift is held?
items.description:
This issue has been systematically fixed in recent builds (virtual-key state is written directly, keymap profiles are corrected automatically, and joystick heartbeats resend input). Normally, moving the stick should move the player.

If it still happens:
1. Under Settings → Controls → Default Control Scheme, check whether the value is "custom" (custom layout).
2. Check whether the in-game key bindings were changed; restore defaults if needed.
3. Update to the latest build and try again; older builds did not include all input fixes.

items.title: What should I know about connecting a Bluetooth mouse or controller?
items.description:
• Bluetooth mouse: Connect or turn it on before launching the game. A mouse enabled mid-game may not be detected (known upstream issue); quit and relaunch the game if this happens.
• Pointer lock: The pointer locks automatically when the game captures the view. Use the "Hide Hardware Pointer" setting as needed.
• Controller: Xbox layout is supported (select it under Settings → Controls → Controller Type). Sticks, triggers, and shoulder buttons have default mappings, which can be customized in Key Bindings.
• Controller drift or detection problems: First confirm that the controller works in system settings, then check that the in-game key bindings have not been cleared.

items.title: How do I edit a custom control layout or restore it if it breaks?
items.description:
Edit: Open the in-game menu → Edit Controls (or select `custom` under Settings → Controls → Default Control Scheme and enter the editor). You can drag and resize controls and add buttons, drawers, or joysticks; save the result as a new layout.

Restore: Select "Restore Default Controls" in the editor. The factory layout will be deleted and recreated; other custom layouts are unaffected. If a damaged layout leaves you with no controls in-game, the launcher automatically falls back to the default layout so the game remains playable.

The factory `custom` layout includes a full drawer with a keyboard icon and commonly used keys. "Restore Default Controls" also installs the latest factory version with corrected key mappings.

items.title: Does the keyboard close after every character in the multiplayer menu? (Confirmed upstream issue; closed)
items.description:
Symptom: In the multiplayer address field, the keyboard closes after every character, so it has to be reopened repeatedly.

Conclusion: This is upstream Minecraft behavior. In 26.x, the multiplayer screen destroys and recreates the text-input context after each character (a Stop→Start cycle). The recreation interval exceeds any debounce window available to the launcher. The launcher has two mitigations (adaptive debounce while typing and persistent allowance for the auto-open input-method switch), but cannot eliminate the interruption caused by upstream recreation. FCL, Zalith, and similar launchers have the same issue. The issue is closed as upstream and should go away when Minecraft fixes text-context management.

Workaround: If the keyboard closes while entering an address, tap the Input Method (✎) button again, or type the address elsewhere (such as Notes) and paste it.

items.title: How should I allocate memory?
items.description:
A typical allocation is up to 50% of the device's total memory (for example, 3 GB on an 8 GB device). With the extended memory-limit entitlement, it can usually be raised to 65%; with extended virtual memory, to 75%.

Other useful settings:
• A view distance of 12 is a good balance; increasing it mainly lengthens chunk-loading spikes and increases memory use.
• For render resolution, prefer an FSR preset over manually lowering the resolution slider.
• When the game stutters, first determine whether chunk loading is slow (switch to Zink, enable FSR, or lower view distance) or the overall frame rate is low (lower view distance, resolution, or shader quality), then adjust accordingly.

items.title: What do the launcher's memory entitlements do?
items.description:
• Extended memory limit: Lets iOS allocate more memory to the launcher, typically increasing its limit by 15%. It can be enabled using an "ID-signing" tool (such as SideStore or NB Assistant) or a paid developer certificate (recommended video: BV1regH6RETM).
• Extended virtual memory: Gives the launcher a larger virtual address space and can typically add another 15% to the limit when combined with the first entitlement. It requires a paid developer certificate (recommended video: BV1regH6RETM).

items.title: Does modpack installation report a missing parent-version JSON?
items.description:
Recent builds can automatically fetch a missing or damaged parent-version JSON during modpack installation from both Mojang's official source and the BMCLAPI mirror. Usually, you do not need to install the vanilla version first.

If it still fails:
1. Check the network (the error appears only if both sources are unreachable).
2. Alternatively, install the matching vanilla version from the Downloads page before installing the modpack.
3. Fully quit and reopen the launcher before trying again.

items.title: How do I install mods, and what if the game crashes or reports incompatibility?
items.description:
Install: Put the `.jar` file in the `mods` folder for the relevant version (with version isolation enabled, use `instance-directory/versions/version-name/mods`). Fabric mods require Fabric Loader first; Forge mods likewise require Forge.

Crash troubleshooting:
1. Check the crash report's "Caused by" and "Mixin apply failed" sections; most crashes are caused by mod-version conflicts or a mismatch with the MC version.
2. Optimization mods (Sodium, Iris, Lithium, etc.) often conflict with one another and with other rendering mods. After adding mods, troubleshoot them one at a time.
3. Do not install two mods that provide the same feature (for example, two minimaps or two optimization packs).
4. If the game still crashes after removing all mods, then investigate the launcher and include the log when reporting the issue.

items.title: Which Java version should I use for each MC version?
items.description:
The launcher automatically chooses the correct Java runtime for the game version; usually, no manual changes are needed:

• MC 26.x → Java 25
• MC 1.20.5–1.21.x → Java 21
• MC 1.17–1.20.4 → Java 17
• MC 1.16.5 and earlier → Java 8

The launcher corrects `javaVersion` values declared by modpack profiles, so incorrect values in older modpacks no longer prevent launch. If manual Forge installation reports a Java-version mismatch, check whether the launcher's Java runtime setting was changed.

items.title: Where is launcher data (worlds, mods, layouts) stored, and how do I back it up?
items.description:
All data is under the app sandbox's Documents directory (`POJAV_HOME`):

• `versions/`: Game versions and isolated mods/configuration.
• `saves/`: Worlds.
• `controlmap/`: Custom control layouts (`default.json` is the default layout and can be edited under Settings → Edit Controls).
• `MG/`: MobileGlues renderer configuration (`config.json`, including the FSR preset).

Backup: Use the Files app or the file manager in the sidebar to copy the entire Documents directory. Restore it to the same location after changing devices or reinstalling. Reinstalling the launcher clears sandbox data, so back up important worlds first.

The `latestlog.txt` log is stored here too; use it when reporting problems.

items.title: Are downloads for versions or resources slow or failing?
items.description:
The launcher uses both Mojang's official source and the BMCLAPI mirror, switching and retrying automatically if a download fails. If downloads remain slow or fail:

1. Check that at least one of `piston-meta.mojang.com` or `bmclapi2.bangbang93.com` is reachable.
2. Check the download-source setting (you can change the preferred source in Settings); BMCLAPI is often preferable on mainland China networks.
3. If the version list fails to load, fully quit and reopen the launcher to fetch it again.
4. If a large file (resource pack/modpack) is interrupted, tap download again to resume or retry; clearing data is unnecessary.

items.title: How do I fix blocks, entities, or clouds appearing transparent or see-through?
items.description:
This is usually a compatibility issue between Sodium's "Improve Transparency" option and the renderer, not a problem with the launcher or world.

Fix: In the in-game Video Settings → Sodium menu, turn off "Improve Transparency" (transparent sorting). The see-through effect should disappear.

This can happen with any renderer, including Zink and MobileGlues; disabling the option is sufficient.

items.title: Are green or corrupted areas appearing after enabling FSR, especially with Zink?
items.description:
Fixed in two rounds. Zink uses the system Vulkan stack, whose shader language (GLSL) is limited to 4.1, while the FSR upscaling shader declared 4.5. Older builds failed compilation and fell back, but did not actually tell the game to restore full-resolution rendering. Only the lower-left area was rendered; the rest showed uninitialized VRAM as large green/corrupted regions.

The two fixes were:
1. Adapt the shader version to Zink's GLSL limit and truly return to full-resolution rendering when upscaling is unavailable (no more green screen).
2. Add missing 4.1 half-precision packing functions and correct the shader-type constant so upscaling works on Zink without fallback.

If green areas still appear, send `latestlog.txt`; it shows which path was used.

items.title: Does the game freeze, go black, or lose frames after switching to the background?
items.description:
This is an iOS restriction on background GPU access, especially visible with Zink (Vulkan). When the app moves to the background, iOS immediately revokes GPU submission access. If the game render thread is still submitting work, the Vulkan device can be permanently lost (logs show `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` or `zink: DEVICE LOST`). On return, the image may be frozen and touch may not respond.

Current advice:
1. Avoid fully switching away from the game. Opening Control Center or Notification Center in split view is usually fine; a full app switch can trigger the issue.
2. If the game freezes, quit and relaunch; a lost Vulkan device cannot be recovered.
3. If you need to switch away frequently (for example, to check a guide), use MobileGlues, whose Metal path handles background transitions better, or use another device.
4. If the image is briefly corrupted after returning but the game remains playable, stale frame-queue contents usually clear after a few seconds.

This is not low memory and the launcher is not killing the process; allocating more memory does not help. Automatic device-loss recovery requires rebuilding the Vulkan device and is on the roadmap.

items.title: How should I report a crash or black screen?
items.description:
The most useful item is `latestlog.txt`, in the launcher's sandbox Documents directory (it can also be viewed from the in-game menu). The latest log is retained after each game session. Include it with:

1. Device model and OS version (for example, iPad Air M4 / iPadOS 26.6).
2. Game version and mod list (for example, 26.3 + Sodium).
3. Renderer and FSR settings.
4. When the problem occurs (entering a world, during gameplay, or after resuming).

Most problems can be diagnosed from the log without a screen recording. Past examples solved from logs include a render-race crash during world loading, chunk-pipeline translation overhead, and Sodium transparent-sorting artifacts.

items.title: What general steps can I try if the game is stuck, spinning, or crashing?
items.description:
Try these steps in order, retrying after each one:

1. Fully quit the launcher (swipe it away) and reopen it; this resolves many temporary state issues.
2. Try another renderer (Zink ↔ MobileGlues) to distinguish a renderer issue from an environment issue.
3. Disable FSR or lower resolution to rule out the upscaling path.
4. Try a new clean world or a version without mods to rule out world and mod issues.
5. If it still fails, send `latestlog.txt` (see above) and say which step you reached and what was on screen.

Do not casually "Clear All Data." Most problems are unrelated to user data, and clearing it loses worlds without fixing the issue.

items.title: Does a large modpack (hundreds of mods) get stuck on its first launch?
items.description:
Typical symptom: The launch overlay or progress screen remains unchanged for several minutes, but the game has not crashed. This is unrelated to renderer choice or memory allocation; adding memory does not help.

Confirmed example (BMC2 modpack, 537 mods): The pack included a desktop-dialog utility mod (`missingmodschecker`) that displays a confirmation when a dependency is missing on desktop. The dialog never appears on iOS, so the main thread waits indefinitely. `[LaunchWatchdog]` in the log identifies the mod where startup is stuck.

The launcher has two protections:
1. It automatically disables confirmed dialog-based mods before launch. `[ModDialogGuard]` appears in the log, and the mod file is renamed to `.disabled`; restore it by changing the extension back to `.jar`.
2. If the main thread makes no progress for 15 seconds, the watchdog records its current code location in `latestlog.txt`. Lines start with `[LaunchWatchdog]`; an `at package.Class` line identifies the stuck mod.

Try:
1. Wait 2–3 minutes; some mods are slow to initialize the first time.
2. Cancel and retry; the first launch copies default modpack files, while the next launch skips that work.
3. If it remains stuck, find the mod named by `[LaunchWatchdog]`, remove it from `mods` (utility mods are often safe to remove), and retry.
4. If the log is unclear, send `latestlog.txt`; the watchdog can pinpoint the problem.

items.title: Does a modpack crash seconds after launch with an LWJGL version incompatibility?
items.description:
Typical symptom: The game exits within seconds rather than hanging, regardless of renderer. Search `latestlog.txt` for `LWJGL version is not compatible`:

Installed version: 3.4.1
Required version: 3.3.1

This is Sodium's pre-launch check. It requires an LWJGL version matching the Minecraft version (for example, 3.3.1 for 1.20.1 and 3.4.1 for 26.x). An older launcher hard-coded 3.4.1 to make 26.x work, which caused Sodium 0.5.13 to reject 1.20.1 modpacks such as BMC2.

Fixed: The launcher now reads the matching LWJGL version from game-version metadata and reports it to Sodium. To verify, search the log for `[Tools] LWJGL report version`; it should show the matching value (1.20.1 → 3.3.1).

If the error persists, install the latest build (check Commit under Settings → About) and send `latestlog.txt`.

items.title: Does a modpack crash halfway through startup with “Could not execute entrypoint stage”?
items.description:
Typical symptom: The mod list is printed and startup advances for about 20–30 seconds, then exits with `exit(-1)`, regardless of renderer. Search `latestlog.txt` for `Could not execute entrypoint stage`; the following `NoClassDefFoundError` / `ClassNotFoundException` chain indicates a missing mod jar, not a renderer or memory issue. A required class (for example, from FTB Library, Balm, or TerraBlender) is not present in `mods`.

Confirmed example (BMC2, 536 mods): More than eight files, including FTB components, Balm, and TerraBlender, failed or were skipped during import. Earlier, `Dependencies overridden for ...` from `config/fabric-loader.json` (`dependencyOverrides`) suppressed Fabric's missing-dependency error, so the problem remained hidden until entrypoint execution.

The launcher has three protections:
1. At the end of import, failed/skipped files are listed in `import_report.json` in the instance directory.
2. On the next launch, unacknowledged missing files trigger a reminder (search the log for `[ImportGuard] Task95`).
3. If the game crashes, the crash screen lists missing classes and inferred component names (such as FTB Quests/Balm).

Try:
1. Remove the instance and re-import it using another download source, or add the named dependency in Mod Manager (use the version required by the modpack).
2. If the log contains `Dependencies overridden for ...`, after fixing the issue remove the `dependencyOverrides` entry from `config/fabric-loader.json` so missing dependencies are reported immediately again.
3. When reporting, attach `latestlog.txt` and the instance-root `import_report.json` to show which files are missing.

items.title: Does a modpack crash late in startup with paintings or sparsestructures errors (listFiles NPE / FileAlreadyExistsException)?
items.description:
Typical symptom: All mods load, then startup exits after about 30–40 seconds during window initialization or resource loading, regardless of renderer. Search for either signature:
1. `NullPointerException` + `Arrays.stream` + `PaintingPackReader.scanPacks` (paintings mod).
2. `FileAlreadyExistsException: config/sparsestructures.json5` (sparsestructures mod).

This was an environment bug in older launcher builds, not a broken mod or missing file. Java resolves relative paths in two ways: `java.io.File` uses the process working directory, while `java.nio` uses `user.dir`. Older builds set only the latter, so the two APIs looked in different directories. paintings checked for a resource-pack folder using one path and listed another, nonexistent directory (causing the null pointer). sparsestructures decided the config file was missing using one path, then tried to create a file that already existed at the actual location.

Fixed in Task97: Before starting the JVM, the launcher aligns the process working directory with the game directory, as on desktop. Verify that the log contains `[CwdAlign] Task97` and `process CWD aligned to game dir: …`. The earlier `Cannot access RandomAccessFile logs/latest.log` error should also disappear because the game can write to the instance's `logs/` directory.

If the error remains after updating, confirm the build includes the Task97 fix (check Commit under Settings → About) and send `latestlog.txt`.

items.title: Does a 26.x Fabric/NeoForge modpack crash seconds after launch with “Loading library SDL” or missing org/lwjgl/sdl/SDL?
items.description:
Typical symptom: A modpack (often a performance pack with Sodium/Iris) exits after printing the mod list and entering vanilla startup. Changing renderers does not help. Log signatures:
1. `Description: Loading library SDL` + `java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: org/lwjgl/sdl/SDL`.
2. An earlier `Failed to get system info for SDL Platform` message (related warning; less severe).

Starting with MC 26.3, windows and input moved from GLFW to SDL3, requiring LWJGL's SDL binding (`lwjgl-sdl`), which is only in the launcher's 3.4.1 set. An older launcher recognized plain version IDs such as `26.3`, but not prefixed modded IDs such as `fabric-loader-0.19.5-26.3-e4ecd7db`, so it incorrectly selected LWJGL 3.3.3, which has no SDL binding. The game then crashed while loading its fifth library (SDL). This is unrelated to the renderer, memory, or Sodium; Sodium's version check has already passed.

Fixed in Task98: Version extraction now ignores prefixes and correctly selects 3.4.1 for Fabric/NeoForge/Forge 26.x. Verify that the log shows `Using LWJGL 341` and the preceding `[LWJGLSel] Task98: MC major 26 extracted from version id …`; SDL should then load normally.

On an older build, update the launcher. As a temporary workaround, set LWJGL to 3.4.1 in Settings → edit the instance.

items.title: Does Minecraft 26.3 crash halfway through startup with “Initializing game” and MacosUtil or NSApplication in the stack trace?
items.description:
Typical symptom: A 26.3 release (including modpacks) exits after mods load and the main window is created, just before gameplay. Log signature:

`java.lang.NoSuchMethodException: Method cannot be found for signature …` with a stack trace through `ca.weblite.objc.Client.sendProxy` → `MacosUtil.disableCloseWindowMenuItem` → `Window.<init>`, and `Description: Initializing game`.

To run LWJGL/JNA on iOS, the launcher identifies as macOS. Minecraft 26.3 then tries to use macOS-only AppKit menu integration during window initialization (disabling the "Close Window" menu through `NSApplication`/`NSMenu`). iOS has UIKit, not AppKit, so class lookup fails and the game crashes. This is unrelated to the renderer, Sodium, or memory; 26.3-rc-3 and earlier did not make this call.

Fixed in two layers (Tasks99 and 100): Before the JVM starts, the Objective-C runtime registers minimal stubs for `NSApplication`, `NSMenu`, and `NSMenuItem`. Task100 added the `windowsMenu`/`appleMenu`/`helpMenu`/`servicesMenu` family after fixing the first issue exposed a second one. Verify `[AppKitStub] Task99: NSApplication/NSMenu/NSMenuItem stubs installed` and `[AppKitStub] Task100: windowsMenu requested` in the log. If an `unexpected selector` appears, send it with `latestlog.txt`; a newer menu API may need a stub.

If using an older build, update the launcher; no in-game setting changes are needed.

items.title: Does a 26.3 modpack crash when entering a world with a Sodium pipeline or preprocessor-directive error?
items.description:
Typical symptom: The main menu works, but the game crashes as soon as you enter a world. The crash report says `Description: Render Frame`, with `Failed to find or load pipeline sodium:pipeline/solid_terrain` as the direct cause.

In 26.x, the rendering frontend compiles GLSL to SPIR-V. Sodium terrain shaders use `#include` to import shared snippets (`globals/fog/chunk_vertex`). Tests showed that Sodium's three snippets do not end with a newline. The launcher's include expander appended the line-restoration directive (`#line`) directly to the last character, producing invalid GLSL and the preprocessor error in the log. Vanilla snippets all end correctly, so hundreds of vanilla shaders compile before the first Sodium shader fails; this is unrelated to the renderer, memory, or LWJGL.

Fixed in Task103: The expander now ensures a trailing newline before appending `#line`. Vanilla shaders are unaffected because they already end correctly. Verify by searching for `[amethyst-include] expanded`; a Sodium shader (such as `sodium:blocks/block_layer_opaque`) should no longer be followed by a GLSL parsing error, and the world should load.

Temporary workaround on older builds: Remove Sodium, Sodium Extra, or Reese's Sodium Options from the modpack. Terrain rendering will fall back to the vanilla pipeline and frame rate may decrease.

items.title: Does a modpack crash while creating a world without a crash report, with the log ending abruptly?
items.description:
Typical symptom: The title screen works, but after selecting "Create New World" the image freezes or the app exits. `latestlog.txt` ends abruptly, with no exit code, crash stack, or `hs_err`; common final lines include spark's `Starting background profiler...` or `[Amethyst] Patching ...libasyncProfiler.so.tmp`.

When a server is first started, spark unpacks its bundled native `libasyncProfiler` into `config/spark/tmp` and loads it. The library is built for macOS and is code-signed. The launcher relabels its platform as iOS, invalidating the signature hash, so the system loader silently kills the process. Changing the platform label is safe for unsigned libraries but fatal for signed ones.

Fixed in two layers (Task106, corrected by Task107): (1) The launcher intercepts this library load; if spark detects failure, it automatically falls back to its pure-Java sampler and the game can continue. (2) General protection recreates an ad-hoc signature after relabeling the platform, recalculating the page hash. Task107 replaced the earlier unsigned-library approach, which caused JNA load failures (`missing code signature`): the system loader rejects unsigned libraries, while re-signing a relabeled signed library allows it to load. Verify `[Amethyst] Task106: blocked dlopen` or `[Amethyst] Task107: re-signed` in the log; if world creation proceeds, the fix is active. Temporary workaround on older builds: remove spark from the modpack.

If the game still exits and the last line is unrelated to spark, check memory. World creation is a memory peak (a measured 537-mod pack used 5.1 GB before creating a world). If device memory is low, the system may silently kill the process; lower the launcher's memory limit or view distance.

items.title: What should I do if the Metal (metallum) renderer crashes in-game?
items.description:
If the game crashes after changing video settings or reloading resources, with a stack trace in the AGXMetalConverter/AGX driver, this is a known issue with the Metal (metallum) backend on some OS versions. The upstream issue is also unfixed, and the launcher cannot work around it.

Temporary workaround: Under Settings → Video → Renderer, switch to ANGLE, gl4es, or MobileGlues (changing renderers does not affect worlds or mods).

The issue where the launch screen required manually tapping "Cancel Launch" is fixed: a Metal first-frame signal now dismisses the overlay automatically when the image appears.

items.title: Does a Forge modpack crash on startup with an IForgeVertexFormat or OptiFine error?
items.description:
If the log shows `java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: net.minecraftforge...IForgeVertexFormat` or a related OptiFine reflection failure, the OptiFine build bundled with the modpack is binary-incompatible with the Forge version (its interface signature has changed). This is a mod issue.

Fix: Remove OptiFine from `mods` or replace it with a build matching that Forge version, then relaunch. When Forge and OptiFine are both detected, the launcher writes a warning marker to the log: `[PojavLauncher] Task202: OptiFine detected alongside Forge`.

Also: If a Forge 26.x launch displays the tiny file dialogs "missing software!" prompt asking whether to open the `early-display-errors` webpage, it is a fallback error dialog after Forge's progress window fails to initialize. iOS has no desktop dialog component, and the console's `y/n` input reaches EOF and is skipped automatically, so startup does not hang. Recent builds disable the Forge progress window by default because it already fails in the translation layer; updating prevents the prompt.
